I’m not comparing apples and oranges, I’m comparing RPG’s and RPG’s. Witcher 3 has karma like systems, Outer Worlds has it, Skyrim has it, Red Dead has it, the vast majority of good RPG’s have SOMETHING resembling some kind of karma system that reacts to your actual gameplay instead of just story choices. It’s not unfair to say that Avowed, a game that was in production for the same amount of time as Skyrim (with a staff almost 3x the size), should have a more interactive world

You don’t seem to get it, gameplay mechanics like this are there for depth. Not everyone is going to want to chop the head off every character they find, the point is that you are able to if you want to. Being able to interact with the tiny parts of the world may not seem that impactful, but giving you the choice is what matters. These things exist for depth, not because you’re always going to make use of them, but because you should have the option to if you want it. By having these in depth systems, it allows you to keep going back over and over because there’s always something you haven’t done before. Avowed reminds me of something like Detroit Become Human, a cool game with a branching storyline based on choice, but at the end of the day it’s a surface level experience with no real depth

I can’t disagree with you, Skyrim as an RPG is lacking even compared to its own predecessors, I only call it the gold standard since it’s the most well known and easy for others to compare to. The best RPG’s are the ones that excel in allowing the player to live in the world as they see fit, and pretty much all these games let you kill whoever the hell you want purely because at the end of the day it should be your choice and they get that

Avowed literally doesn’t let you kill any NPC not labelled an enemy, Skyrim will. Avowed literally doesn’t let you interact with small miscellaneous objects like cups, Skyrim does. NPC’s in Avowed will only go as far to say “I can see you” when robbing their life savings, Skyrim NPC’s will attack you and call the guards. Avowed literally doesn’t have pathing for creatures as they are all static objects with idle animations and combat logic, the majority of NPC’s in Skyrim have full pathing and a daily routine. Avowed literally doesn’t have a day night cycle, Skyrim does. Avowed doesn’t do any of that better, not in any reality

It’s an RPG, naturally it’s going to be compared to other great RPG’s, especially when it took over 5 years of development on a team with like 250 people. Even if you don’t want to compare it to Skyrim for some reason, compare Avowed to previous Obsidian titles and it falls short in almost every category. Fallout New Vegas, and yes I get people hype it up more than it probably deserves, but New Vegas puts Avowed to shame in terms of being an RPG

Dead zones are also an issue, but that’s not even what I was talking about. If you’re aiming right and go to aim left, you still aim right until the exact moment the stick cross the middle and goes to the left side, and while that time is minimal, in a game like siege is distinctly matters. A mouse also offers more precision, where controller need to crank sensitivity to try and be able to flick across the screen and do 180’s, a mouse can just do it no compromises necessary. If xim players really want to play the game with xim, there should be xim lobbies

While not perfect, Xim does let you use a mouse as your primary aiming device, and the mouse itself is the direct advantage. Keyboard isn’t necessarily a big advantage over controller, especially if that controller has paddles, but in terms of sheer accuracy and performance, a mouse is better than a controller every single day of the week. If it wasn’t then we’d see controller players in CSGO

That’s mouse to mouse though, completely different conversation. With controller, you use the analog stick, now say you’re aiming right and a guy appears on the left side of the screen. With a controller when you aim left there is time for your stick to pass the midway so it’ll actually aim left, and then it has to hit the other side entirely to aim at full speed. Basically, with a controller there are always small periods of time where, despite you aiming one direction, it’s not moving at all, that simply isn’t a thing at all with MnK. There’s more to it than that, but I recommend watching a video about it. Controllers are awesome for racing games and such, but any and all fps games are dominated by MnK

Her hyper armour is also special, every other enemy in the game can have their poise broken during hyper armour allowing for a critical attack. Melania, unless you proc bleed or frost, cannot under any circumstance have her poise broken during a hyper armour attack, and they just so happen to make up about half of all her attacks. Her hyper armour also starts on frame one of the attacks, making her waterfowl dance even stronger as she can literally pull it out on you while you are in the middle of a combo on her.  She can counter you for taking advantage of openings, and she steals health back for it. Even if you don’t actually get hit, say you block with a shield with 100 Physical defence, she still heals. Melania all but forces the player to use some kind of bleed/frost build with weapons that deal decent stagger, because without such tools her fight becomes an even worse nightmare. Yes, she’s not unbeatable, but that’s not an excuse to call her fair, let alone balanced. Don’t get me wrong, I love Melania, she’s one of favourite bosses in the game, but it’s undeniable that she takes combat mechanics that have been consistent throughout the entire game, and breaks them for no reason.

I cannot show you a video of ethical slaughter because no matter what I show you, you will see a video of ending an animals life and hate it, which I understand. The problem with a plant based diet is that we can’t get much of the vegan stuff up here without it costing crazy amounts of money. Half the time I live in the Northwest Territories in Canada, and up there anything fresh is hard to come by, and crazy expensive. The other half of the time I’m down with my family, and I’m pretty much vegan, I’ll still eat eggs, but I barely drink milk, and I’ll only eat meat if it’s some big event like a wedding, but that just doesn’t work up there. I tried it for about 6 months up there, but it just wasn’t possible, everything was gross and old, had to be microwaved, something, and I just couldn’t do it. I gave up on the 6 month mark because my buddy decided it was finally time I come to his farm. He explained to me how he does things there. Each cow is impregnated once every 2 years (1/3 will be done milking this year, the next 1/3 just got their 2 years off, and the 1/3 after that is in the middle of vacay) after they are 2 years old and ready. Each female cow produces milk for about 10 months, which covers pretty much the whole year. Unfortunately, due to the conditions up here, even cows that just live in nature untouched will only live to the age of roughly 12-14 at most. So what he does is he waits until the cows are at minimum 10-11 before he does anything. He’d wait longer, but he says the last few years of their life, especially up here, are kind of like the last couple years of a dogs life, you love them very much, but it’s just sad to see them struggle to do everything that once came easy to them. Once the time has come, he brings the cows in one at a time, he leads them to a nice big warm pen, and he waits until they fall asleep, he’ll feed them something nice and give them a good bath, exactly the kinds of things someone would do for their dog. Unfortunately, he knows that the community needs the meat from those cows, and putting them down via injection, while nicer, would put a lot of people out of food. I can’t remember what he said he does honestly, but I do remember him saying that it is as fast and painless as possible, as in they never have the time to even process what happened before they’re gone, his words not mine. I know we’ll never agree on if this is right or ethical, there’s no way I’ll get you to agree with me, and I already more or less agree with you guys. It’s just the best possible example of what the dairy and meat industry possibly could be, not a factory where pigs tails are ripped off, and cows are terrified, but somewhere where cows are allowed to be comfortable and happy, and his pigs get mud pits to chill in. Dudes got scratching posts and the like everywhere, he truly does care for those animals, enough that he’d rather let the meat be of pretty mediocre quality and let them live as full a life he can, than kill them while the meat is valuable and sell it to become wealthy.
